Self-test hygiene: (a) a new seat-selftest mutant in dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py takes a per-file id (for example cloud_relay-1), never a new S number (the P6 convention), and sits inside the block of the instrument it tests, never appended at the file's end, so parallel additions touch different hunks; on 2026-10-21 three pull requests (R10-FLOW-RELAY-HOLD, R10-FLOW-YIELD-PROBE, R10-CI-LAYOUT's PR G) each lost a code round to a content conflict there when main gained tick_loop mutants S31-S34. (b) A self-test builds any git repository through tests/throwaway_git.py, never a hand-built git init (a pusher-reap handoff was refused for exactly that in tools/audit/seat/pr_args.sh); run python3 tests/throwaway_git.py --check before the handoff. (c) Any new git push site is registered in PUSHERS in tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py in the same pull request, or ref_privacy refuses it (#2582's heartbeat push did). (d) The body's Red checks section answers every check red on main's ancestry, one line each (today nightly-status), or pr-contract refuses it (standing rule 22).

Revision 12 (orchestrator, 2026-10-21): (1) the reviewer prompt requires every observation in the first verdict to carry 'Carry: <group>' or 'Carry: dismissed <reason>', so pre-flight's carry gate never parks a merge verdict on an unmarked note (it parked #2576, #2567 and #2571, each a fresh Opus re-verdict); (2) refuse a reviewer at a head that shares a hot file (pr_args.sh, update_pr.sh, cloud_relay.sh, orchestrator_tick.py, r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py) with an open pull request that holds an unboarded merge verdict: that one boards first, and this one is reviewed after absorbing it, so a paid verdict is never killed by a content conflict (#2567 went DIRTY after its 16:21Z verdict).
brief: One call per cloud seat (Lean flow study K16; expedite since revision 4: the repo half has no dependency on any other flow group, and its cost recurs for every seat). Today each cloud seat costs a rendered payload plus two trigger bodies pasted whole, and the renderer needs environment, model and repo flags and refuses host paths. Make cloud_dispatch.py take only role, group and model, derive the rest from the roster and the seat environment it already knows, write the rendered brief to a ref the seat fetches, and print the one short line the trigger needs (the ref name), so a standing trigger per role can be fired with that line alone. Whether the trigger tool can take a file or a ref is the owner's harness, not this repo; the group builds the repo half. Controls: a fixture dispatch renders the same payload as today's three-step path, byte for byte; a host path still refuses; the printed line round-trips to the brief. The dispatcher refuses a reviewer dispatch for a head where a required context's latest run has concluded failure (revision 7: #2563 was dispatched for review at 9851d39d with two required checks red), reading R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE's classifier.
